metric: mean fraction of the concrete indicators the agent asserted (IPs, hashes, CVEs, MITRE techniques, domains) that appear in the evidence it was handed, over a deterministic prefix of services/agents/tests/eval_data/synthetic_incidents.json. An incident whose investigation fails outright (raises, or returns status=failed) scores 0 with the reason recorded in the report's groundedness.zero_scored block, so the sample size always equals the dispatched prefix — dropping failures is survivor bias, and the shrunken sample fails this gate's own size requirement.
served_by: Ollama, locally. No hosted provider was involved in any run below and this floor describes none. A hosted model would need its own runs and its own floor.

derivation: Two significant figures of history. The original floor was set from the pre-fix harness: seven local runs at 0.5561 and three GitHub-runner runs spread 0.5329-0.5933, with 0.40 chosen 0.1329 below the lowest. Those runs are kept above for provenance but they describe a harness with two defects fixed in the same change as this re-derivation (#1466): per-incident asyncio.run poisoned langchain-openai's cached async HTTP client, so recon ran its deterministic fallback on every incident after the first (llm_calls 62 vs 74-78 now), and an incident whose investigation failed was dropped, inflating the mean and shrinking the sample below what this gate requires. Under the fixed harness (one loop per run, failures scored 0 with reasons recorded) the observed means are 0.51, 0.445 and 0.44 locally and 0.5234 re-expressed from the two identical CI runs that motivated the fix. The floor stays 0.40: it sits below the lowest run cited anywhere (0.44), and the thinner margin is deliberate rather than accidental — one failed investigation costs the mean about 0.05 under zero-fill, so a run with three or more outright failures dips below the floor and reds the job, which is exactly the signal a reader should get from a model failing a third of its investigations. Raise or move it only with fresh runs recorded here; a floor above the lowest cited run is refused by scripts/check_live_agent_floor.py.
